name: Ourasphaira
fact: The oldest known fungus: a tangle of tiny threads with round swellings, a billion years old. Its cell walls contain chitin, the same tough material as in mushrooms today. Fungi are close cousins of animals.
know: Scientists dissolved the rock in acid to free the fossils, then used light to read the chemistry of their walls: the signal of chitin, which algae do not make.

name: Proterocladus
fact: A green seaweed about a billion years old, with branching threads divided into cells. It is the oldest known member of the green algae — the group that later gave rise to every land plant.

name: Possible sponge (Little Dal reefs)
size: Tubes a fraction of a millimetre wide
fact: A network of tiny tubes inside reefs built by microbes, 890 million years old. It looks like the skeleton of a sponge. If it is one, animals are about 350 million years older than the first clear fossils.
debate: Networks like this can also form in other ways, and no chemical traces of sponges are known from rocks this old. Many scientists are not convinced.
sites: Little Dal Group, Mackenzie Mountains, Canada

name: Vase-shaped microfossils
fact: Single cells that built tiny vase-shaped shells to live in, like some amoebae in ponds today. They are among the oldest fossils of cells that ate other cells.
